thm-normalized-degree-two-spherical-char.title: Benedict H. Gross, On the Satake isomorphism
thm-normalized-degree-two-spherical-char.locator: §1, local setting and definition of the Weyl group on PDF page 2, and invariants after (1.4). §2, (2.1)–(2.5), the double-coset basis before Proposition 2.6, and (2.11)–(2.13). §3, (3.1)–(3.5) and Proposition 3.6. §6, the complex isomorphism preceding (6.3).
thm-normalized-degree-two-spherical-char.statement: The integral spherical Hecke ring consists of locally constant, compactly supported, integer-valued bi-K-invariant functions. The double-coset indicators form its integral basis, and convolution for Haar measure giving K volume one is its multiplication, with the indicator of K as unit. The normalized Satake transform has value at each t in the diagonal torus equal to the positive square root of the modulus at t times the integral over N of n ↦ f(tn). After complex scalar extension it is a unital algebra isomorphism onto the Weyl-invariant group algebra of the diagonal torus modulo its intersection with K. For the split torus, quotient by its integral points gives the cocharacter lattice, where the cocharacters are algebraic group homomorphisms from the multiplicative group to the torus. Evaluation at the uniformizer followed by passage to the quotient inverts that identification. The Weyl group is the quotient of the normalizer of the torus by the torus.
thm-normalized-degree-two-spherical-char.hypotheses: A nonarchimedean local field with finite residue field and a chosen uniformizer, and a connected split reductive group with an integral group scheme model of reductive special fiber. A split maximal torus is contained in a Borel, both defined over the valuation ring. The compact subgroup K consists of the integral points of the model, and N consists of the field points of the unipotent radical of the Borel. The Haar measures give K and N ∩ K volume one, respectively. The local application uses the standard degree-two matrix model.
thm-normalized-degree-two-spherical-char.reading_limits: Read the cited setting, integral Hecke ring, torus identification, normalized isomorphism and its complex version. The example (3.7) assumes dominant cocharacters. The proof here computes the coefficients for all valuation pairs from (3.4) and identifies the complex source algebra.

This measure then defines the measure on the quotient by the discrete image of the rational units.

thm-euler-weight-two-satake-unitarity.title: Andrew Corbett and Abhishek Saha, On the order of vanishing of newforms at cusps
thm-euler-weight-two-satake-unitarity.locator: §2.1.1, definition of U₀ (p. 6), §§2.1.4–2.1.5, equation (8) and the least-exponent rule (p. 8), §2.1.8, Definition 2.9 (p. 10), §3.1, (20)–(22) (pp. 16–17), §§3.2.1–3.2.2, Lemma 3.1 and the normalization after (25) (pp. 17–18), and §3.2.3, (28) and the following sentence (p. 19).
thm-euler-weight-two-satake-unitarity.statement: An irreducible unitary cuspidal representation of GL₂ over the rational adeles of the specified real type contains an adelic newform invariant by the product of its local K₁ groups at the least fixed-vector exponents. At positive exponent n, K₁(n) uses c ≡ 0 and a ≡ 1, while K′₁(n) uses c ≡ 0 and d ≡ 1. The literal local test in equation (8) at exponent zero uses U₀ equal to the unit group, so it requires a unit upper-left entry. The global level subgroup in §3.1 uses the full integral factor at unramified primes. The associated classical holomorphic newform has weight k and level given by the product of the prime powers of those exponents. Equation (22) gives the determinant-normalized restriction of the adelic newform to real matrices of positive determinant. Equation (21) prescribes the character exp(ikθ) for the rotation with first row (cos θ, sin θ). The normalization following (25) sets the first Fourier coefficient to one. The additive quotient of the adeles by Q is compact and uses invariant probability measure. The global Whittaker newform factors with a local Whittaker newform belonging to every finite factor. The smooth finite factors are thus generic, meaning they have a nonzero Whittaker functional. At each finite place the local newform is a nonzero fixed vector at the least congruence exponent.
thm-euler-weight-two-satake-unitarity.hypotheses: The global representation is irreducible unitary cuspidal over Q and its central character is trivial on the positive real scalars. The full real factor is the discrete series of lowest weight k, defined in §3.1 as the unique irreducible subrepresentation of normalized induction from |·|^((k−1)/2) sgn^k and |·|^((1−k)/2). Here k=2, so the sign factor is trivial. The local conductor definition uses irreducible admissible generic smooth factors, as used for the given cuspidal representation in §3.1.
thm-euler-weight-two-satake-unitarity.reading_limits: Read the listed congruence, correspondence, normalization, and local and global Whittaker passages. The correspondence, genericity and local newvector existence are used as stated. Equality of the fixed spaces at zero, transport at positive exponents and the determinant twist are supplied locally.

thm-euler-weight-two-satake-unitarity.title: Denis Trotabas, Modular Forms and Automorphic Representations
thm-euler-weight-two-satake-unitarity.statement: An irreducible unitary representation of GL₂ of the rational adeles is the restricted Hilbert tensor product of irreducible unitary local factors with unit spherical reference vectors outside a finite set. The Hilbert space is the completion of the span of elementary tensors agreeing with the reference vectors outside finitely many places, with the product inner product on elementary tensors. Its restriction to a single place is a Hilbert direct sum of copies of that factor, which determines the local equivalence class. At a finite place an irreducible unitary representation has finite-dimensional fixed spaces for each compact open subgroup, and its smooth vectors form an irreducible admissible representation.
thm-euler-weight-two-satake-unitarity.hypotheses: The tensor-product assertion is for an irreducible unitary representation of GL₂ over the rational adeles. The local admissibility theorem is for an irreducible unitary representation of a reductive group over a local field, and the smooth-vector assertion uses the nonarchimedean case and admissibility. Here the local group is GL₂(Q_q).
thm-euler-weight-two-satake-unitarity.reading_limits: Read the tensor construction and restriction remark, the tensor-product theorem statement and the finite-place admissibility and smooth-vector passages. The representation-theoretic existence and admissibility results are used as stated.

thm-euler-weight-two-satake-unitarity.title: Denis Trotabas, Modular Forms and Automorphic Representations
thm-euler-weight-two-satake-unitarity.locator: §§8.1–8.2 (pp. 25–27), especially the hypotheses of §8.1 and the pairing and continuity argument on p. 27.
thm-euler-weight-two-satake-unitarity.statement: The central-character Hilbert space consists of Borel representatives modulo almost-everywhere equality on the rational quotient, with Borel descended moduli and squared norm integrated on the central quotient. For GL₂ over the rational adeles the central quotient has finite volume. The cuspidal subspace is the intersection of the kernels of continuous linear functionals defined by compactly supported tests on the left quotient by the adelic upper unitriangular group. On a smooth representative the functional integrates the unipotent constant term against its test.
thm-euler-weight-two-satake-unitarity.hypotheses: The central-character model uses a locally compact unimodular group, closed unimodular subgroups for the measured quotients, and a unitary central character trivial on the rational scalars. The pairing example is for GL₂ over the rational adeles with the compact additive rational-to-adelic quotient and the finite-volume central quotient.
thm-euler-weight-two-satake-unitarity.reading_limits: Read the conventions in §8.1 and the pairing formula, finite-volume assertion, continuity statement and closed-kernel characterization in §8.2. The application uses the continuity and pairing identity and needs only inclusion of the smooth cuspidal closure.

thm-euler-weight-two-satake-unitarity.title: Jayce R. Getz and Heekyoung Hahn, An Introduction to Automorphic Representations
thm-euler-weight-two-satake-unitarity.locator: §2.3, Proposition 2.3.1 and the preceding restricted-product construction (pp. 47–48), §§3.1–3.2 including Theorem 3.2.2 (p. 72), and §3.6, Lemma 3.6.4 and the paragraph following its proof (pp. 78–79). Also §4.4, the isotypic decomposition, Proposition 4.4.3 and Theorem 4.4.6 (pp. 102, 104), §4.6, the construction around (4.15), Theorem 4.6.1 and Proposition 4.6.2 (pp. 108–110), and §4.8, Definition 4.7 (p. 112).
thm-euler-weight-two-satake-unitarity.statement: An affine algebraic group's adelic points form a locally compact Hausdorff group with the restricted-product topology, and its rational points form a closed discrete subgroup. The adelic group is unimodular for a reductive group. A closed subgroup whose modular function equals the restriction of the ambient modular function admits a nonzero right-invariant Radon measure on the left coset space, unique up to positive scale and induced by the quotient Haar integral formula. Every locally compact Hausdorff group has a nonzero positive Radon right Haar measure, unique up to positive scaling. Abelian and discrete locally compact groups are unimodular. For a unitary representation of a real reductive group, the Hilbert space is the orthogonal Hilbert sum of its compact isotypic subspaces. In a Hilbert representation the vectors that are both smooth and compact-finite are dense and stable under the Lie algebra. Irreducible unitary representations are unitarily equivalent if their underlying modules are isomorphic by a map intertwining both the Lie algebra and maximal compact group actions. For a complex reductive Lie algebra with a chosen Cartan subalgebra, a Harish–Chandra parameter evaluates the Cartan projection of a central enveloping-algebra element after the shift by the half-sum of positive roots. An essentially square-integrable representation has square-integrable coefficients on the subgroup cut out by absolute values of rational characters, which for real GL₂ is the group of matrices of absolute determinant one.
thm-euler-weight-two-satake-unitarity.hypotheses: The adelic assertions are over a global field, here Q. The topology and discreteness are used for GL₂ and GL₄, with the integral matrix groups as restricted-product factors, and reductivity is used for GL₂. The quotient theorem requires a locally compact group and a closed subgroup with matching modular functions. Haar existence applies to a locally compact Hausdorff group. The abelian and discrete cases apply to the center and the indicated rational and unipotent subgroups. The archimedean assertions concern real reductive groups and use a maximal compact subgroup. The unitary equivalence assertion requires irreducible unitary representations whose underlying modules are isomorphic for the joint Lie algebra and maximal compact group actions. The Harish–Chandra formula applies to a module with an infinitesimal character, with the diagonal Cartan subalgebra in the application to complexified real GL₂.
thm-euler-weight-two-satake-unitarity.reading_limits: Read the statements and restricted-product description at the stated locators. The closedness and unimodularity of the product with the full adelic center are checked in the proof. The evaluation on the scalar generator and integration of its infinitesimal action are carried out below.

thm-euler-weight-two-satake-unitarity.title: Toshiyuki Kobayashi and Birgit Speh, How does the restriction of representations change under translations? A story for the general linear groups and the unitary groups

def-author-e2fc0f4318ab-normalized-weigh.title: Computing classical modular forms
def-author-e2fc0f4318ab-normalized-weigh.locator: §4.1, pp. 6–7, Eqs. (4.1.1), (4.1.4), (4.1.6) and the paragraph beginning “The above spaces can be equipped”. §6.1, pp. 18–19, opening hypotheses, Hecke formula, and the paragraphs on normalized newforms and on $f_{M_1,j}^{M_2}$.
def-author-e2fc0f4318ab-normalized-weigh.statement: The subgroup $\Gamma_1(N)$ consists of matrices in $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)$ with $a\equiv d\equiv1$ and $c\equiv0\pmod N$. A fixed-character form transforms on $\Gamma_0(N)$ by the slash multiplier $\epsilon(d)$. A normalized cuspidal newform is in the new subspace, has first coefficient one and is an eigenform for the operators $T_m$ indexed by all positive integers $m$. The lower-level images in the cuspidal basis are $f_{M_1,j}(M_2z)$ for $M_1M_2\mid N$ with the character conductor dividing $M_1$. The classical operator on the cusp space is $T_m f=m^{-1}\sum_{ad=m,\ \gcd(a,N)=1}\chi(a)a^k\sum_{b\bmod d} f((az+b)/d)$.
def-author-e2fc0f4318ab-normalized-weigh.hypotheses: Positive integral level $N$ and weight $k$. In §6.1 the character comes from a primitive character of conductor $Q\mid N$ with $\chi(-1)=(-1)^k$. The fixed-character space uses its induced character on units modulo $N$. The Hecke formula acts on this cusp space for every positive integer $m$.
def-author-e2fc0f4318ab-normalized-weigh.reading_limits: Checked the cited passages for the subgroup, normalization, scope of the newform eigencondition, lower-level maps and Hecke formula. At $k=2$, $a^2/m=m/d^2$ when $ad=m$, and extending the level character by zero allows all positive factorizations. The local argument uses the formula and conventions for newforms, with no basis theorem used.

def-author-e2fc0f4318ab-normalized-weigh.title: Fred Diamond and John Im, Modular forms and modular curves
def-author-e2fc0f4318ab-normalized-weigh.locator: §2.1, p. 42, the congruence-subgroup and cusp-form definitions. Remark 3.4.2 and §3.5, Proposition 3.5.1, pp. 52–53. §3.6, p. 54, Eq. (3.6.1). §6.1, Eq. (6.1.1), Remark 6.1.2 and the fixed-character paragraphs before Remark 6.1.3, pp. 60–61. §6.3, p. 63, the discussion and definition after Corollary 6.3.1.
def-author-e2fc0f4318ab-normalized-weigh.statement: The congruence subgroup $\Gamma_1(N)$ is defined by $a\equiv d\equiv1$ and $c\equiv0\pmod N$ in $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)$. A form on a congruence subgroup is cuspidal if every determinant-one slash transform vanishes at infinity. On forms common to the spaces with and without the fixed-character notation the $T_m$ actions agree. For weight $k\ge2$ the image of the full Hecke ring on $M_k(\Gamma_1(N))$ is generated by all $T_m$ for $m\ge1$. The old subspace of $S_k(N,\epsilon)$ is the span of the images of $g(z)\mapsto t^{k-1}g(tz)$ from $S_k(M,\epsilon_M)$ as $M$ ranges over proper divisors of $N$ divisible by the conductor of $\epsilon$, $\epsilon_M$ induces $\epsilon$, and $t\mid N/M$. The new subspace is its orthogonal complement for the Petersson product. If $P=\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb Z)$ and $\overline{\Gamma}$ is the image of the congruence subgroup $\Gamma$ in $P$, the Petersson product integrates $f(z)\overline{g(z)}y^k$ against $dx\,dy/y^2$ over a fundamental region and divides by $[P:\overline{\Gamma}]$. A normalized eigenform for the full Hecke ring in the new subspace has $a_1=1$ and is called a newform or a primitive cusp form.
def-author-e2fc0f4318ab-normalized-weigh.hypotheses: The application uses weight two and positive integral level $N$. The Hecke generation statement requires $k\ge2$. For the pairing, $f$ and $g$ are cusp forms on the congruence subgroup in the normalizing factor. The fixed-character construction uses a Dirichlet character modulo $N$ and its pullback description from level $M$ on units. The full Hecke eigenform convention is for the new subspace of $S_k(\Gamma_1(N))$, including its fixed-character subspaces.
def-author-e2fc0f4318ab-normalized-weigh.reading_limits: Checked the cited definitions and conventions in extracts from the PDF, including the projective denominator in Eq. (3.6.1). The paragraph after Lemma 3.6.1 writes the translate count using the unprojectivized subgroup notation. Steps 3.2 and 5.1 derive the count for the effective actions used here. thm-author-f93d28423212-greaves-prime-pa.title: On the representation of a number in the form x² + y² + p² + q² where p, q are odd primes
thm-author-f93d28423212-greaves-prime-pa.locator: Acta Arithmetica 29 (1976), §1, theorem, survivor comparison and convention on implied constants; (3.1), Lemma 7, (4.1), Lemma 8, (4.13)–(4.14), and §6, (6.1)
thm-author-f93d28423212-greaves-prime-pa.statement: For sufficiently large N in an allowed class, the ordered prime pairs with 1 < p,q ≤ √(N/2) for which N−p²−q² is a sum of two integer squares number more than A(N)N(1+e_N)/(log N)^(5/2), with A(N) from (6.1) and |e_N| bounded by L log log N/(log N)^(1/10). The lower bound in §6 comes from subtracting unwanted survivors among the ordered prime pairs.
thm-author-f93d28423212-greaves-prime-pa.hypotheses: N is a sufficiently large positive integer incongruent to 0, 1 and 5 modulo 8. Count a pair when at least one representation of its remainder as a sum of two integer squares exists. The constant L may depend at most on N modulo 8.
thm-author-f93d28423212-greaves-prime-pa.reading_limits: Read the indexed text of the theorem and its survivor comparison, the ordered-pair setup, Lemmas 7 and 8 and the conclusion. The index renders the radical inconsistently. The bound at √(N/2) uses the range in (4.1) and Lemma 8, consistent with N=2Z² in Lemma 7, and the conclusion via (4.13)–(4.14). Page images could not be retrieved. The sieve estimates are imported and the threshold is existential.

thm-author-f93d28423212-greaves-prime-pa.title: On the representation of a number in the form x² + y² + p² + q² where p, q are odd primes
thm-author-f93d28423212-greaves-prime-pa.locator: Acta Arithmetica 29 (1976), (2.4), §3 preceding (3.4), (3.4)–(3.6), (4.6), Lemma 10, and §6 through (6.1)
thm-author-f93d28423212-greaves-prime-pa.statement: A(N)=D B G Π₀/√2 with D>0 given by (2.4) independently of N and B=Kψ(K,1)/φ(K)²>0, where K is a positive divisor of 72 and ψ(K,1) comes from the normalized residue-pair count (3.4). The positive G is determined by C/B in the function g of §6. Lemma 10 gives C/B as a fixed positive multiple of (φ(K)/K)².
thm-author-f93d28423212-greaves-prime-pa.hypotheses: N lies in one of the five classes in the theorem. Take K and the residue restrictions from Greaves's construction in §§3–4 and the constants from the same construction in §§5–6.
thm-author-f93d28423212-greaves-prime-pa.reading_limits: Checked the indexed coefficient formulas and positivity statements in the passages cited. The dependence on K suffices here and the numerical multiplier in Lemma 10 is unused. The sieve derivation is imported.

thm-author-f93d28423212-greaves-prime-pa.title: On the representation of a number in the form x² + y² + p² + q² where p, q are odd primes
thm-author-f93d28423212-greaves-prime-pa.locator: Acta Arithmetica 29 (1976), end of §1, (3.4)–(3.7), (4.4), (4.9) and following sentence, and (4.11)–(4.12)
thm-author-f93d28423212-greaves-prime-pa.statement: Π₀ is the convergent product over primes ℓ≡3 modulo 4 of (1−τ(ℓ)/ℓ)/(1−1/ℓ), with τ(ℓ)<ℓ. For ℓ>3 not dividing N, τ(ℓ)=1+O(1/ℓ), with the implied constant depending at most on N modulo 8. For ℓ≡3 modulo 4 dividing N, τ(ℓ)=0. For fixed ℓ, τ(ℓ) is determined by K, ℓ, the totients and the normalized counts from (3.4)–(3.7) at l=1 and l=ℓ.
thm-author-f93d28423212-greaves-prime-pa.hypotheses: Use the sieve for Greaves's set of odd-prime pairs in §§3–4 and N in the stated classes modulo 8. The large-prime estimate is used only for ℓ>3 with ℓ not dividing N.
thm-author-f93d28423212-greaves-prime-pa.reading_limits: Checked the indexed local-count setup, the bounds on τ and the convergence statement. The proof below uses the finite moduli and the stated bounds to derive a uniform positive lower bound.

lem-author-c3a9b9243c74-compact-projecti.title: John Voight, Quaternion Algebras, Chapter 27: Adelic framework
lem-author-c3a9b9243c74-compact-projecti.locator: Corollary 27.6.20 (division-algebra case) and §27.6 opening hypotheses, with Lemma 27.6.8 for class equivalence, §27.4.1 for eligible places and §27.5.4 for the ring of integers specialization.
lem-author-c3a9b9243c74-compact-projecti.statement: For a finite-dimensional division algebra B over a global field F and an R-order O in B, the locally principal right fractional O-ideals form a finite set of classes under left multiplication by B×. For a number field and the set S of all archimedean places, the ring of S-integers is its ring of integers.
lem-author-c3a9b9243c74-compact-projecti.hypotheses: R is the ring of S-integers of F for a finite nonempty set S containing all archimedean places. Here F is Q, S consists of the real place and R is Z. The proof verifies that B is a division algebra and O is a full Z-order.
lem-author-c3a9b9243c74-compact-projecti.reading_limits: Checked the cited passages in the publisher HTML, including the corollary's short proof and the class equivalence in Lemma 27.6.8. The corollary uses Main Theorem 27.6.14, whose proof invokes an adelic bound on differences of elements in translates of a compact set. Class-set finiteness is used as a published premise here.

lem-author-c3a9b9243c74-compact-projecti.title: John Voight, Quaternion Algebras, Chapter 14: Quaternion algebras over global fields
lem-author-c3a9b9243c74-compact-projecti.statement: A finite extension of Q is a number field and a global field. The places of Q are its unique archimedean place, given by the usual real absolute value, and the nonarchimedean places indexed by the rational primes, given by the corresponding p-adic absolute values.
lem-author-c3a9b9243c74-compact-projecti.hypotheses: The place classification is for the rational field Q.
lem-author-c3a9b9243c74-compact-projecti.reading_limits: Checked the definition and classification statement in the publisher HTML. Only the global-field condition and the archimedean part of the classification are used here.

def-author-f98bf83ef432-local-k-one-subg.title: Andrew Corbett and Abhishek Saha, On the order of vanishing of newforms at cusps
def-author-f98bf83ef432-local-k-one-subg.locator: §2.1.1 (PDF page 6), §2.1.4 equation (8) and §2.1.5 (PDF page 8), §3.1 up to equation (22) (PDF pages 16–17)
def-author-f98bf83ef432-local-k-one-subg.statement: Section 2.1.1 defines a uniformizer as a generator of the maximal ideal of $\mathfrak o$. For $K=\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathfrak o)$ and $n\ge 0$, equation (8) defines $K_1(n)$ by $c\in\varpi^n\mathfrak o$ and $a\in U_n$, and $K'_1(n)$ by $c\in\varpi^n\mathfrak o$ and $d\in U_n$. Here $U_n=1+\varpi^n\mathfrak o$ for $n>0$ and $U_0=\mathfrak o^\times$. Section 2.1.1 normalizes $|\varpi|=1/\#(\mathfrak o/\varpi\mathfrak o)$. Section 2.1.5 defines the conductor exponent using the unprimed group. Section 3.1 uses these unprimed local factors for the adelic newform and uses $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb Z_p)$ at each prime $p$ of exponent zero.
def-author-f98bf83ef432-local-k-one-subg.hypotheses: For the local subgroup definitions, $F$ is a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero with ring of integers $\mathfrak o$ and uniformizer $\varpi$. Section 2.1.5 defines the conductor for irreducible admissible generic representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$. The adelic setting of §3.1 is over $\mathbb Q$, with an irreducible unitary cuspidal representation, central character trivial on the positive reals, and a holomorphic discrete series of lowest weight $k\ge2$ at infinity.
def-author-f98bf83ef432-local-k-one-subg.reading_limits: Checked the PDF text for the uniformizer definition, absolute value normalization, unit filtration, two matrix groups, choice of fixed subgroup for the conductor, and the local factors used in the adelic newform construction. def-author-f98bf83ef432-local-conductor-.title: Andrew Corbett and Abhishek Saha, On the order of vanishing of newforms at cusps
def-author-f98bf83ef432-local-conductor-.locator: General notation and §2.1.1, p. 6, continuity and unit filtration. §2.1.3, p. 7, the fixed additive character. §2.1.4, equation (8), and §2.1.5, p. 8, the local conductor. §3.1, p. 16, the adelic product.
def-author-f98bf83ef432-local-conductor-.statement: Inside $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathfrak o)$, equation (8) defines $K_1(n)$ by $c\in\varpi^n\mathfrak o$ and $a\in U_n$, and $K'_1(n)$ by $c\in\varpi^n\mathfrak o$ and $d\in U_n$. Here $U_n=1+\varpi^n\mathfrak o$ for $n>0$ and $U_0=\mathfrak o^\times$. The absolute value is normalized by $|\varpi|=\#(\mathfrak o/\varpi\mathfrak o)^{-1}$. The authors fix a continuous additive character trivial on $\mathfrak o$ and nontrivial on $\varpi^{-1}\mathfrak o$. Section 2.1.5 defines the conductor exponent using the least nonnegative index at which $K_1(n)$ fixes a nonzero vector. The local factors of the adelic congruence subgroup in §3.1 are $K_1(n)$ at positive index and $\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb Z_q)$ at index zero.
def-author-f98bf83ef432-local-conductor-.hypotheses: The local passages use a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic zero with ring of integers $\mathfrak o$ and uniformizer $\varpi$. Section 2.1.5 treats irreducible, admissible, generic local representations. Section 3.1 works over $\mathbb Q$ with an irreducible unitary cuspidal automorphic representation whose central character is trivial on the positive reals and whose real factor has holomorphic discrete-series lowest weight $k\ge2$.
def-author-f98bf83ef432-local-conductor-.reading_limits: Checked the stated passages for the normalization, the unit filtration, the fixed character, the matrix conditions, the local conductor and the adelic product. The comparison assumes existence of a qualifying index and uses the local subgroup argument.

def-author-f98bf83ef432-local-conductor-.title: J. S. Milne, Algebraic Number Theory
def-author-f98bf83ef432-local-conductor-.locator: Version 3.08, Chapter 7, paragraph after Proposition 7.5 (PDF page 109) and Proposition 7.46 and Definition 7.48 (PDF page 128).
def-author-f98bf83ef432-local-conductor-.statement: An absolute value is discrete when the absolute values of the nonzero elements form a discrete multiplicative subgroup of the positive reals. For a field complete for a discrete absolute value, the ring of integers is compact if and only if its residue field is finite. A field with a nontrivial absolute value is a local field if it is locally compact in the induced topology, in which case it is also complete.
def-author-f98bf83ef432-local-conductor-.hypotheses: The discreteness criterion uses the nonzero values in the positive reals with their usual topology. Proposition 7.46 assumes completeness for a discrete absolute value, with the ring of integers and its residue field taken for that absolute value. Definition 7.48 requires a field with a nontrivial absolute value and local compactness for the induced metric topology.
def-author-f98bf83ef432-local-conductor-.reading_limits: Read the paragraph after Proposition 7.5, the statement and proof of Proposition 7.46, and Definition 7.48 in the PDF text. The argument uses the finite-residue-field direction and checks discreteness and local compactness for the q-adic field.

def-author-f98bf83ef432-local-conductor-.title: Torsten Wedhorn, The Local Langlands Correspondence for GL(n) over p-adic Fields
def-author-f98bf83ef432-local-conductor-.statement: With its local group topology, $\mathrm{GL}_n(K)$ is a locally compact Hausdorff group. The compact open subgroups $I+\pi_K^m M_n(\mathcal O_K)$, $m\ge1$, form a neighbourhood basis at the identity. Admissibility requires open vector stabilizers and finite-dimensional spaces of fixed vectors for open subgroups. In the smooth category the finite-dimensional condition is equivalent to testing compact open subgroups. For a smooth irreducible representation of $\mathrm{GL}_n(K)$, genericity is nonvanishing of $\operatorname{Hom}_{U_n(K)}(V,\theta_\psi)$ for the upper unitriangular group, where $\theta_\psi(u)=\psi(\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}u_{i,i+1})$. Genericity is independent of the choice of nontrivial additive character $\psi$.
def-author-f98bf83ef432-local-conductor-.hypotheses: The notations take $K$ to be a finite extension of $\mathbb Q_p$, $\mathcal O_K$ its ring of integers and $\pi_K$ a uniformizer. Section 2.1 treats the group of points of a connected reductive group and explicitly includes $\mathrm{GL}_n(K)$. Section 2.4 uses a smooth irreducible complex representation of $\mathrm{GL}_n(K)$ and a nontrivial continuous additive character of $K$ into the unit circle.
def-author-f98bf83ef432-local-conductor-.reading_limits: Checked the PDF text for the standing notation, the identity neighbourhood basis, admissibility, genericity and character independence. The entry topology and the unit modulus condition for characters of $\mathbb Q_q$ are checked locally.
